subject: Procurement pathway + approval map for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jared Phillips <jared.phillips@acme-retail.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Procurement pathway + approval map for Redwood pilot

Hi Samantha —

Great to meet you and Jared on the call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align procurement and legal: 

Summary of current state:
- Acme is interested in a 3-month pilot (1-2k tokens/day avg) for in-store recommendations and search re-ranking.
- Primary procurement questions: PO vs card, marketplace procurement (AWS/GCP marketplace), and standard Redwood T&Cs.
- Economic buyer appears to be Jared (Head of Product); finance sponsor is Samantha in Procurement.

Action items I have for you:
1) Confirm whether Acme requires a PO or if a corporate card is acceptable for the pilot.
2) Share any internal procurement form / supplier setup checklist (vendor name, tax ID, W9 if US).
3) Confirm signatory path (who signs the SOW / MSA) and whether legal redlines go to in-house counsel or procurement.
4) Indicate if AWS Marketplace purchase would speed approval (we can list there and provide marketplace pricing + invoice flow).

What I can provide immediately:
- Draft SOW and starter contract (attached: Redwood_SOW_Draft.docx).
- Standard procurement questionnaire (I can fill in and return).
- Quick pricing options: card-based monthly or net-30 PO billing for reserved capacity.

Would you be able to reply with: PO vs card, procurement contact email for vendor setup, and expected internal timeline? If helpful, we can do a 15-min sync with procurement this week.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the loop so we can schedule a pilot start date.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Phillips <jared.phillips@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Procurement pathway + approval map for Redwood pilot

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a couple of notes from procurement: 

1) PO vs Card: For pilots under $10k we sometimes allow purchase via corporate card, but our standard is PO/net-30 for anything tied to proof-of-value followed by production. Because this is a pilot that may convert to a contract, procurement will prefer a PO.

2) Supplier setup: I attached our PO template and vendor onboarding spreadsheet. We’ll need Redwood’s legal name, W9, DBAs, and certificate of insurance. (See Acme_PO_Template.pdf).

3) Signatory path: Jared is the economic buyer and will approve spend. The final signatory for the MSA is our VP Operations (I will confirm name). Legal redlines can be shared with our counsel; procurement handles commercial terms first.

4) Marketplace: Yes — if Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace with invoice-on-behalf (IOB) enabled, it shortens approvals because we can purchase directly through Marketplace billing. That’s often the fastest route.

Expected timeline: vendor setup + PO issuance ~2–3 weeks once we receive the completed vendor form and W9.

I’m attaching the PO template and a small procurement checklist. I can run a 15-min call with Jared and me if you want to walk through the onboarding fields.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager | Acme Retail
samantha.lee@acme-retail.com

Attachments: Acme_PO_Template.pdf, Procurement_Qs.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jared Phillips <jared.phillips@acme-retail.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Procurement pathway + approval map for Redwood pilot

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Samantha. Helpful notes — a couple clarifying points and next steps from our side: 

Clarifications:
- We can accept PO/net-30. For pilots we typically offer an invoice schedule aligned to usage (monthly).
- AWS Marketplace listing: we do have a listing in process; I will confirm if IOB is enabled by Thursday.

Immediate next steps (for coordination):
- I’ll send a filled vendor form + W9 and a draft SOW updated with the pilot scope by EOD Tuesday.
- Dev (cc) will provide a short technical appendix for the SOW describing data flows and security controls.
- Lauren (cc, finance) — can you confirm if Redwood’s standard net-30 is acceptable for our quote and whether we can provide a 30-day invoice-to-PO conversion if they start on card?

Proposed Pilot commercial options to make procurement comfortable (choose one):
A) PO + Net-30: Redwood invoices monthly against PO, pilot capped at $8k total.
B) Card to start + PO if converted to production within 30 days (we issue refund/credit adjustments as needed).
C) Marketplace (if IOB enabled): Purchase via AWS marketplace, handles invoicing and can accelerate approval.

Would you and Jared be able to indicate a preferred option? If PO, please send the vendor onboarding fields we should populate.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOW and the technical appendix.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: Redwood_SOW_Draft.docx (updated to include pilot cap)

Subject: Re: Procurement pathway + approval map for Redwood pilot — Tech appendix + pricing guidance

Marissa / team —

Draft tech appendix for the SOW (summary):
- Data flow: client-side anonymized product IDs -> signed request to Redwood hosted inference -> token-limited responses. No PII stored.
- Security: TLS in transit, optional VPC peering for Private deployment if required. SOC2 controls mapped in the appendix.
- Capacity: pilot configured on shared-hosted with 2x concurrency; auto-scale options described.

Pricing guidance (for Marissa to present to procurement):
- Card-based pilot: $6,000 flat for the 3-month pilot (fixed cap).
- PO/net-30 pilot: $7,500 total (includes small admin surcharge).
- Marketplace list price: $8,000 with marketplace fees included (IOB speeds approval).

DocuSign link (for standard SOW/MSA): https://www.docusign.com/REDWOOD-SIGN-12345

I attached a short appendix and the procurement Qs I recommend we pre-fill.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
